analysis.evidence: וַיְהִי introduces the scene. הַשֶּׁמֶשׁ לָבוֹא sets the time, “as the sun was about to set,” and וְתַרְדֵּמָה נָפְלָה עַל אַבְרָם tells what happened, “a deep sleep fell on Abram.”
analysis.morphology: The prefixed conjunction וַ is followed by יְהִי, the short third-person masculine singular Qal form of הָיָה used in the wayyiqtol.

analysis.evidence: הַשֶּׁמֶשׁ לָבוֹא means “the sun was about to set,” fixing the time when a deep sleep fell on Abram.
analysis.morphology: The definite article הַ doubles the initial שׁ of the noun. The noun is common gender, singular, and in the absolute state.

analysis.evidence: הַשֶּׁמֶשׁ is the subject. וַיְהִי הַשֶּׁמֶשׁ לָבוֹא means “as the sun was about to set” and gives the time when deep sleep fell on Abram.
analysis.morphology: The preposition לָ־ introduces a Qal infinitive construct.

analysis.evidence: תַרְדֵּמָה is the subject of the feminine singular verb נָפְלָה. As the sun was setting, a deep sleep fell upon Abram (עַל אַבְרָם).
analysis.morphology: The conjunction וְ joins the clause to the preceding one. The noun is common, feminine singular, in the absolute state.

analysis.evidence: תַרְדֵּמָה ‘deep sleep’ is the subject of נָפְלָה, and עַל אַבְרָם identifies whom it came over. The clause reads ‘a deep sleep fell upon Abram’.
analysis.morphology: Qal perfect, third person feminine singular, agreeing with תַרְדֵּמָה ‘deep sleep’.
analysis.sense: fall upon, come over (of deep sleep)

analysis.evidence: In וְתַרְדֵּמָה נָפְלָה עַל אַבְרָם, “a deep sleep fell upon Abram,” עַל introduces the person upon whom the sleep fell. The verse echoes this construction in נֹפֶלֶת עָלָיו, “falling upon him.”
analysis.morphology: Hebrew preposition without a prefix or suffix. Its object is אַבְרָם.

draft.change: Link the existing Abram article to אבה through its father element and add Genesis 12:4 as an example.
draft.definition: Abram, son of Terah, later named Abraham. The name means “exalted father.”
draft.evidence: Genesis 12:4 repeats the name אַבְרָם when giving Abram’s age at departure. The name’s אָב element belongs to Haqor’s אבה article.

analysis.evidence: In נָפְלָה עַל אַבְרָם, Abram is the person upon whom a deep sleep fell. The following עָלָיו (“upon him”) refers back to Abram.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew personal name with no prefix or suffix. The preceding preposition עַל is a separate word.
analysis.sense: Abram, the son of Terah later named Abraham

analysis.evidence: Carried forward: this word and its source tagging were reviewed identically at 69380:0, 69379:7, 67597:18, 67595:5, 67084:4, 65823:6.
analysis.morphology: Conjunction וְ prefixed to the presentative particle הִנֵּה.
analysis.sense: and there was (what one sees or finds)

analysis.evidence: As the sun is setting and a deep sleep falls on Abram, אֵימָה names the dread that falls upon him (נֹפֶלֶת עָלָיו) in association with great darkness (חֲשֵׁכָה גְדֹלָה).
analysis.morphology: Feminine singular common noun in the absolute state, with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: As the sun is setting, חֲשֵׁכָה גְדֹלָה describes a great darkness falling on Abram. אֵימָה supplies the accompanying sense of dread, and גְדֹלָה describes the darkness as great.
analysis.morphology: Common noun, feminine singular absolute, with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: In אֵימָה חֲשֵׁכָה גְדֹלָה, both אֵימָה ‘dread’ and חֲשֵׁכָה ‘darkness’ are feminine singular. גְדֹלָה expresses the intensity of the experience that falls upon Abram.
analysis.morphology: Attributive adjective, feminine singular absolute, with no prefix or pronominal suffix.
